name: Amy Klobuchar
role: U.S. Senator from Minnesota (2007-present); 2020 presidential candidate
summary: Klobuchar is a mainstream Democrat whose Senate record favors a higher minimum wage, financial and antitrust regulation, marriage equality, abortion rights and voting-rights legislation. She has voted for surveillance extensions, police funding and border-enforcement measures, and backs Ukraine and NATO.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted yea on the $15 minimum wage amendment (2021), the $17 amendment (2025), the Fair Minimum Wage Act (2007) and the 2014 Minimum Wage Fairness Act cloture.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted yea on Dodd-Frank financial regulation (2010) and on the 2013 amendment to end Too Big To Fail subsidies.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted yea on the TARP bailout (2008) and nay on 2009 amendments to end TARP spending and to bar auto-maker bailouts.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted yea on the 2013 Manchin-Toomey background check amendment.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted yea on the 2011 PATRIOT Act extension and the 2012 FISA Amendments Act extension, but also yea in 2020 on the amendment barring FISA collection of browsing history.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Voted yea on the 2015 McCain-Feinstein amendment reaffirming the ban on torture.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted yea on the Respect for Marriage Act (2022) and on ENDA (2013).

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted yea on cloture for the Women's Health Protection Act (2022) and nay on measures to defund Planned Parenthood.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Voted yea on the 2013 Employment Non-Discrimination Act, which bars employers from discriminating on sexual orientation or gender identity.

voter-id.rationale: Voted nay in June 2026 on S2, a bill requiring proof of citizenship and photo ID to vote; the bill bundles other provisions.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Voted yea on 2025 resolutions ending the tariff emergency declared by the President.

collective-defense.rationale: Spoke in support of Finland and Sweden joining NATO in 2022.

arms-reduction.rationale: Voted yea on the New START treaty (2010).

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Voted yea on the 2025 amendment to restore international disaster assistance.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted yea on the 2013 comprehensive immigration reform bill, but also for the 2025 Laken Riley Act detention amendments; the record leans away from tight restriction.

open-borders.rationale: Voted yea on border-enforcement amendments (2025) and on bills that pair legalization with border security; no vote for open borders.

death-penalty.rationale: Said in 2012 that terrorists should be subject to the death penalty.

rehabilitation.rationale: Spoke for the First Step Act, backing reduced mandatory minimums and rehabilitation for low-level nonviolent offenders.

unions-good.rationale: Voted nay on 2012 amendments limiting union dues and Davis-Bacon wage rules.

voluntary-union-payments-at-work.rationale: Voted nay in 2012 on the amendment on workers' right not to subsidize union activities.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Voted yea on 2021 amendments to fund police and hire 100,000 officers.

limit-campaign-donations.rationale: Backs the DISCLOSE Act and Freedom to Vote Act and says Citizens United opened the floodgates to special-interest money.

corporate-influence.rationale: Argues in antitrust speeches that concentrated corporate power harms consumers and workers.

single-official-language.rationale: Voted yea in 2007 on the amendment declaring English the national language of the government.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted yea in 2025 on the amendment eliminating the federal scholarship program for private and religious schools.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted nay on the 2014 bill and 2012 amendment approving the Keystone XL pipeline and nay in 2022 on approving coal leases.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Voted yea on the Employment Non-Discrimination Act (2013), the Respect for Marriage Act (2022) and the 2009 Lilly Ledbetter Act, all laws extending equal treatment before the law.

separated-powers.rationale: Argued in 2026 floor speeches that Congress must reassert its war powers against the President.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wrote in 2019 that racism and sexism persist and are reflected in our laws and our institutions.
